mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up this journey together, just take a moment to notice where you’ve come from. You’ve walked alongside stories of struggle and hope—stories where grace showed up in the mess, pushed past shame, and invited every person, no matter their past, into a life of real freedom and belonging. It’s not about chasing perfection. It’s about learning to trust, deep down, that you’re already held, already loved, already enough. So here’s what stands out: Grace isn’t something you have to earn, and it’s not something you can lose. It’s a steady, unshakeable gift. Even when you’re sitting with regret or failure, acceptance is still possible. Forgiveness—real forgiveness—frees your heart, even if the past can’t be changed. Relationships? They come alive when you give grace as freely as you’ve received it. And as you lean into trust, hope and freedom start to take root, because love just won’t let go. Now, as you head back into the rhythm of everyday life, keep this close: grace isn’t some distant ideal or a prize for those who get it right. It’s here, right now, alive in every moment, every relationship, every setback and fresh start. You don’t have to have it all together. No need to hide your flaws, or wear a mask. The grip of grace is strong enough to hold you, gentle enough to heal you, and wide enough to include everyone you meet. So, let this truth shape you. See yourself and others through the lens of grace. Offer it freely, just like it’s been given to you. When shame whispers that you’re not enough, remember—grace says you are. When fear tries to hold you back, let grace give you courage. And if you ever wonder whether hope is really possible, trust that grace is already at work, opening up a way forward. You’re not alone. You’re not beyond hope. You are, and always will be, in the grip of grace. Go ahead—live like it’s true. Because it is.
